standard_prerequisites.name: Eigenvariable condition for the False-forall rule
standard_prerequisites.statement: From False (forall x A(x)) the False-forall rule derives False A(c) for a constant c that does not occur above the inserted line in the tableau.
standard_prerequisites.use: The inserted line False A(c) is a correct rule application exactly because c does not occur in the assumptions B_1,...,B_n nor in forall x A(x).

standard_prerequisites.name: Derivability via closed tableaux
standard_prerequisites.statement: Gamma proves A iff for some finite B_1,...,B_n in Gamma the set {False A, True B_1,...,True B_n} has a closed tableau.
standard_prerequisites.use: The hypothesis unpacks into a closed witness tableau whose first assumption is replaced in the construction.

core_obligations: Statement (lines 1223-1227): if c is a constant not occurring in Gamma or A(x) and Gamma proves A(c), then Gamma proves forall x A(x).

Witness transformation (proof lines 1229-1241): take the closed tableau for {False A(c), True B_1,...,True B_n}, replace the first assumption with False (forall x A(x)), and insert False A(c) directly after the assumptions.

Correctness of the insertion (proof lines 1256-1259): the tableau is still closed since every sentence available as an assumption before remains available at the top of the new tableau; the inserted line is a correct application of the False-forall rule because c does not occur in B_1,...,B_n or in forall x A(x), i.e. it does not occur above the inserted line.
proof_roadmap: Unpack Gamma proves A(c) into its closed witness tableau.
Replace the first assumption by False (forall x A(x)) and reinsert False A(c) after the assumptions.
Verify closure carries over and the eigenvariable condition makes the inserted line correct.
